records.arabic: ذكره بن هشام في مختصر السيرة عمن يثق به من أهل العلم عن بن شهاب عن عبيد الله عن بن عباس في تسمية من أعطاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غنائم حنين قال بن إسحاق وأعطى السهمي خمسين من الإبل قال بن هشام اسمه عدي بن قيس وروى بن مردويه من طريق بكر بن بكار عن علي بن المبارك عن يحيى بن أبي كثير في تسمية المؤلفة عدي بن قيس السهمي
records.english: Ibn Hishām mentioned him in his abridgment of the Sīrah from someone he trusted among the scholars, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, in naming those to whom the Prophet ﷺ gave from the spoils of Ḥunayn. Ibn Isḥāq said: He gave the Sahmī fifty camels. Ibn Hishām said: His name was ʿAdī ibn Qays. Ibn Mardawayh narrated by way of Bakr ibn Bakkār, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, in naming those whose hearts were reconciled: ʿAdī ibn Qays al-Sahmī.

names.arabic: عدي بن قيس بن حذافة السهمي
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Qays ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: عدي بن قيس بن حذافة السهمي
title.english: ʿAdī ibn Qays ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī

records.arabic: لا أعرف نسبه وقع ذكره في حديث غريب روى المعافى في الجليس من طريق محمد بن أبي بكر الأنصاري عن عبادة بن الصامت قال بعثني أبو بكر إلى ملك الروم ومعي عمرو بن العاص وأخوه هشام وعدي بن كعب ونعيم بن عبد الله فخرجنا حتى قدمنا على جبلة بن الأيهم بدمشق فذكر قصة طويلة في ورقتين وإسناده ضعيف وقد أخرجهما البيهقي في الدلائل من وجه آخر كما سيأتي في ترجمة هشام بن العاص ويحتمل أن يكون عدي بن كعب هذا هو أبو خيثمة والد سليمان فقد سماه الأزدي كذلك فالله أعلم
records.english: I do not know his lineage; he was mentioned in an unusual report that al-Muʿāfā transmitted in al-Jalīs, by way of Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Anṣārī, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, who said: “Abū Bakr sent me to the king of the Romans. With me were ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, his brother Hishām, ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, and Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh. We set out until we came to Jabalah ibn al-Ayham in Damascus.” He then related a long story occupying two folios. Its chain is weak. Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it by another route in al-Dalāʾil, as will appear in the biography of Hishām ibn al-ʿĀṣ. This ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb may be Abū Khaythamah, the father of Sulaymān, for al-Azdī named him as such. فالله أعلم

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن خباب بن عدي بن الجد بن العجلان البلوي حليف الأنصار استشهد يوم خيبر طعن بين ثدييه بحربة فمات منها ذكره أبو عمر
records.english: ibn Khabbāb ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Jadd ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Balawī, an ally of the Anṣār. He was martyred on the day of Khaybar. He was stabbed between the breasts with a spear and died from it. Abū ʿUmar mentioned him.

aliases: ʿAdī ibn Murrah ibn Surāqah ibn Khubāb ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Jadd ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Balawī
names.arabic: عدي بن مرة بن سراقة بن خباب بن عدي بن الجد بن العجلان البلوي
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Murrah ibn Surāqah — ibn Khabbāb ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Jadd ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Balawī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو نضيلة بالتصغير بن عبد العزي بن حرثان بن عوف بن عبيد بن عويج بن عدي بن كعب القرشي العدوي ويقال عدي بن أسد ذكره بن إسحاق في مهاجرة الحبشة وقال موسى بن عقبة عدي بن أسد العدوي مات بالحبشة وهو أول موروث في الإسلام ورثه ابنه النعمان قلت فخالف بن إسحاق في نسبه وفي أوليته فإن بن إسحاق قال إن أول موروث في الإسلام المطلب بن أزهر فورثه ابنه عبد الله كما تقدم ووافق موسى الزبير بن بكار فقال مات نضلة بن عدي بالحبشة وورثه ابنه النعمان وهو أول من ورث بالإسلام ويمكن الجمع بأن يكون أولية المطلب بالحجاز وأولية النعمان بالحبشة
records.english: or Nuḍaylah, in the diminutive, ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ḥarthān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUwayj ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, the Qurashī and ʿAdawī. He is also called ʿAdī ibn Asad. Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him among those who emigrated to Abyssinia. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: “ʿAdī ibn Asad al-ʿAdawī died in Abyssinia. He was the first person inherited from in Islam; his son al-Nuʿmān inherited from him.” I say: He differed from Ibn Isḥāq concerning his lineage and concerning his priority, for Ibn Isḥāq said that the first person inherited from in Islam was al-Muṭṭalib ibn Azhar, whom his son ʿAbd Allāh inherited from, as was discussed previously. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār agreed with Mūsā, saying: “Naḍlah ibn ʿAdī died in Abyssinia and his son al-Nuʿmān inherited from him. He was the first person inherited from under Islam.” The accounts can be reconciled by taking al-Muṭṭalib's priority to apply to the Hijaz and al-Nuʿmān's to Abyssinia.

names.arabic: بن عبد العزي بن حرثان بن عوف بن عبيد بن عويج بن عدي بن كعب
names.english: ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ḥarthān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUwayj ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
أخو ورقة وهو الأصغر ذكره الزبير بن بكار في النسب وقال أمه آمنة بنت جابر أخت تأبط شرا الشاعر أسلم يوم الفتح وعمل على حضرموت لعمر أو لعثمان قال وأرسل إلى زوجته أم عبد الله بنت أبي البختري لتسير إليه فلم تفعل فقال
إذا ما أم عبد الله لم تحلل بواديه
ولم تمس قريبا هيج الشوق دواعيه قال الزبير بن بكار وكانت دار عدي بن نوفل بالمدينة بين المسجد والسوق عند البلاط وهي التي يعني الشاعر بقوله
إن ممشاك نحو دار عدي
كان للقلب شهوة وقوتا قال فقال لها أخوها الأسود قد بلغ الأمر من بن عمك ارحلي إليه فتوجهت قال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني تفرد الزبير بنسبة هذا الشعر لعدي وأما أبو عمر الشيباني وأبو عبد الله بن الأعرابي ومن تبعهما فقالوا إنه للنعمان بن بشير
records.english: brother of Waraqah; he was the younger one. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned him in al-Nasab and said: His mother was Āminah bint Jābir, the sister of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran the poet. He embraced Islam on the Day of the Conquest and served as governor of Ḥaḍramawt for ʿUmar or ʿUthmān. He said: He sent for his wife, Umm ʿAbd Allāh bint Abī al-Bakhtarī, to travel to him, but she did not. He said: “Whenever Umm ʿAbd Allāh does not alight in his valley and spend the night nearby, yearning stirs its summons.” Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: ʿAdī ibn Nawfal's house in Medina was between the mosque and the market, by the paved area. It is the house intended by the poet's words: “Indeed, your walking toward the house of ʿAdī was desire and nourishment for the heart.” He said: Her brother al-Aswad said to her, “Your paternal cousin's condition has reached this point; travel to him.” So she set out. Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī said: Al-Zubayr alone attributed this poetry to ʿAdī. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aʿrābī, and those who followed them said that it was by al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr.

names.arabic: عدي بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزي
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā

names.arabic: أم عبد الله بنت أبي البختري
names.english: Umm ʿAbd Allāh bint Abī al-Bakhtarī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: عدي بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزي القرشي الأسدي
title.english: ʿAdī ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā al-Qurashī al-Asadī

records.arabic: بن معاوية بن جبلة بن عدي بن ربيعة بن معاوية الأكرمين الكندي يكنى أبا وهب ذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء في ترجمة الوليد بن عدي ابنه وقال كان أبوه عدي ممن وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Jabalah ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Akramīn al-Kindī, whose kunyah was Abū Wahb. Al-Marzubānī mentioned him in Muʿjam al-Shuʿarāʾ in the biography of his son al-Walīd ibn ʿAdī and said: His father ʿAdī was among those who came to the Prophet ﷺ as delegates.

names.arabic: عدي بن هانئ بن حجر بن معاوية بن جبلة بن عدي بن ربيعة بن معاوية الأكرمين الكندي
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Hāniʾ ibn Ḥujr ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Jabalah ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Akramīn al-Kindī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن حجر بن عدي بن ربيعة بن معاوية بن الحارث بن معاوية الأكرمين أبو عائذ استدركه بن الدباغ وقال وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بن الكلبي وكذا استدركه بن فتحون
records.english: ibn Ḥujr ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Akramīn, Abū ʿĀʾidh. Ibn al-Dabbāgh supplied him as an omission and said: He came to the Prophet ﷺ as a delegate. Ibn al-Kalbī said this. Ibn Fatḥūn likewise supplied him as an omission.

names.arabic: عدي بن همام بن مرة بن حجر بن عدي بن ربيعة بن معاوية بن الحارث بن معاوية الأكرمين
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Hammām ibn Murrah ibn Ḥujr ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Akramīn

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بن الحارث بن مالك بن فهم بن غنم بن دوس الدوسي ذكره أبو حاتم السجستاني في المعمرين وقال عاش ثلاثمائة سنة وأدرك الإسلام فاسلم وغزا وقال في ذلك
لا عيش إلا الجنة المخضره
من يدخل النار ملاق ضره قلت العقي بكسر المهملة بعدها قاف ساكنة
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik ibn Fahm ibn Ghanm ibn Daws, the Dawsī. Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī mentioned him in al-Muʿammarīn and said: He lived three hundred years, reached Islam, embraced it, and went on campaign. He said concerning that: “There is no life except verdant Paradise; whoever enters the Fire will meet its harm.” I say: Al-ʿUqī has the unpointed letter bearing a kasrah, followed by a vowelless qāf.

aliases: ʿAdī ibn Wadāʿ ibn al-ʿUqī ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik ibn Fahm ibn Ghanm ibn Daws
names.arabic: عدي بن وداع بن العقي بن الحارث بن مالك بن فهم بن غنم بن دوس
names.english: ʿAdī ibn Wadāʿ ibn al-ʿUqay — ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik ibn Fahm ibn Ghanm ibn Daws

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي والإسماعيلي وأخرج من طريق الوازع بن نافع عن أبي سلمة عن عدي التيمي سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول تقوم الساعة على حثالة الناس قال البغوي لا أعلمه إلا من هذا الوجه وفي إسناده الوازع وهو ضعيف جدا واستدركه أبو موسى
records.english: al-Baghawī and al-Ismāʿīlī mentioned him and transmitted through al-Wāziʿ ibn Nāfiʿ, from Abū Salamah, from ʿAdī al-Taymī: “I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: ‘The Hour will come upon the dregs of mankind.’” Al-Baghawī said: I know it only by this route. In its chain is al-Wāziʿ, who is very weak. Abū Mūsā supplied him as an omission.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: يقال إنه بن زيد ويقال غيره وفرق بينهما البغوي والطبراني وأخرج من طريق حفص بن ميسرة عن عبد الرحمن بن حرملة عن عدي الجذامي أنه لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض أسفاره قلت يا رسول الله كانت لي امرأتان اقتتلتا فرمت إحداهما الأخرى فماتت قال اعقلها ولا ترثها قال وكأني أنظر إليه على ناقة حمراء وهو يقول تعلموا أيها الناس فإنما الأيدي ثلاثة الحديث وهكذا أخرجه سعيد بن منصور عن حفص وأورد بن منده هذا الحديث في ترجمة عدي بن زيد وقال إن حفص بن ميسرة أرسله فقد رواه محمد بن فليح عن عبد الرحمن بن حرملة عن سعيد بن المسيب عن عدي بن زيد قلت هي رواية الحسن بن سفيان في مسنده من هذا الوجه قال ورواه سعيد بن أبي هلال عن عبد الرحمن عن رجل من جذام عن أبيه ورواه يحيى بن أيوب عن عبد الرحمن حدثني رجل من أهل الشام عن رجل منهم يقال له عدي قلت ورواه عبد الرزاق في مصنفه عن محمد بن يحيى المازني عن عبد الرحمن أنه سمع رجلا من جذام عن رجل منهم يقال له عدي بن زيد قلت الراجح من هذه الروايات هذه الأخيرة الموافقة لاللتين قبلها وبها يترجح أنه زيد بن عدي الماضي ويحتمل أن يكون غيره وافق اسمه أبيه العين بعدها الراء
records.english: it is said he was ibn Zayd, or another man; al-Baghawī distinguished the two and al-Ṭabarānī distinguished between them and transmitted by way of Ḥafṣ ibn Maysarah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, from ʿAdī al-Judhāmī, that he met the Messenger of God ﷺ on one of his journeys. “I said: ‘O Messenger of God, I had two wives who fought. One threw something at the other, and she died.’ He said: ‘Pay her blood money, but do not inherit from her.’ It is as though I can see him upon a red she-camel, saying: ‘Learn, O people, for hands are only three types,’” followed by the hadith. Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr likewise transmitted it from Ḥafṣ. Ibn Mandah included this hadith in the biography of ʿAdī ibn Zayd and said that Ḥafṣ ibn Maysarah transmitted it without a Companion in the chain, for Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAdī ibn Zayd. I say: This is al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān's narration in his Musnad by this route. He said: Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from a man of Judhām, from his father. Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: “A man of the people of Syria related to me, from one of their men called ʿAdī.” I say: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated it in his Muṣannaf from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that he heard a man of Judhām, from one of their men called ʿAdī ibn Zayd. I say: The last of these narrations, agreeing with the two before it, is the more likely. By it, the view that he is the previously mentioned Zayd ibn ʿAdī gains strength. He may instead be another man whose name agreed with his father's name. The letter ʿayn followed by rāʾ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بفتح أوله والراء الخفيفة وبعد الألف موحدة بن أوس بن قيظي بن عمرو بن زيد بن جشم بن حارثة بن الحارث الأوسي ثم الحارثي قال بن حبان له صحبة وقال بن إسحاق استصغره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو والبراء بن عازب وغير واحد فردهم يوم أحد وأخرجه البخاري في تاريخه من طريق بن إسحاق حدثني الزهري عن عروة بن الزبير بذلك قال بن سعد كان عرابة مشهورا بالجود وله أخبار مع معاوية وفيه يقول الشماخ
إذا ما راية رفعت لمجد
تلقاها عرابة باليمين الأبيات وسبب ذلك بما ذكره المبرد وغيره أن عرابة لقي الشماخ وهو يريد المدينة فسأله ما أقدمه فقال أردت أن أمتار لأهلي وكان معه بعيران فأوقرهما برا وتمرا وكساه وأكرمه فخرج عن المدينة وامتدحه بالقصيدة المذكورة
records.english: with fatḥah on the first letter and a light rāʾ, followed by bāʾ after the alif; ibn Aws ibn Qayẓī ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn Jusham ibn Ḥārithah ibn al-Ḥārith, the Awsī and then Ḥārithī. Ibn Ḥibbān said: He had companionship. Ibn Isḥāq said: The Prophet ﷺ deemed him, al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, and several others too young and sent them back on the day of Uḥud. Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Tārīkh by way of Ibn Isḥāq: Al-Zuhrī related to me, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning that. Ibn Saʿd said: ʿArābah was famous for generosity and had stories with Muʿāwiyah. Al-Shammākh said concerning him: “Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArābah receives it with his right hand,” followed by the verses. The reason for this, as al-Mubarrad and others mentioned, was that ʿArābah met al-Shammākh while he was heading for Medina and asked what had brought him. He replied, “I wanted to obtain provisions for my family.” He had two camels, so ʿArābah loaded them with wheat and dates, clothed him, and treated him generously. Al-Shammākh left Medina and praised him in the poem mentioned.

names.arabic: بن أوس بن قيظي بن عمرو بن زيد بن جشم بن حارثة بن الحارث
names.english: ibn Aws ibn Qayẓī ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn Jusham ibn Ḥārithah ibn al-Ḥārith

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: استدركه بن الدباغ وقال شهد في الكتاب الذي كتبه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للعلاء بن الحضرمي حين بعثه إلى البحرين
records.english: Ibn al-Dabbāgh added him and said he witnessed the writing in which the Prophet ﷺ wrote for al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī when he sent him to Bahrain.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال أبو موسى له ذكر في إسناد كذا أخرجه مختصرا
records.english: Abū Mūsā said he was mentioned in a chain; this is how it was transmitted in abbreviated form.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بكسر أوله وسكون الراء بعدها موحدة وبعد الألف معجمة بن سارية السلمي أبو نجيح صحابي مشهور من أهل الصفة هو ممن نزل فيه قوله تعالى ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم وقال أيضا كل واحد من عمرو بن عبسة والعرباض بن سارية أنا رابع الإسلام لا يدري أيهما قبل صاحبه ثم نزل حمص وحديثه في السنن الأربعة روى عنه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح وعنه أبو أمامة الباهلي وعبد الرحمن بن عائذ وجبير بن نفير وحجر بن حجر الكلاعي وسعيد بن هانئ الخولاني وشريح بن عبيد وعبد الله بن أبي بلال وأبو رهم السماعي وغير واحد وقال محمد بن عوف كان قديم الإسلام جدا قال خليفة مات في فتنة بن الزبير وقال أبو مسهر مات بعد ذلك سنة خمس وسبعين وفي الطبراني من طريق عروة بن رويم عن العرباض بن سارية وكان شيخا كبيرا من الصحابة
records.english: with kasrah on the first letter, quiescence on rāʾ, then bāʾ and a pointed ḍād after the alif; ibn Sāriyah al-Sulamī, Abū Najīḥ. He was a well-known Companion and one of the people of the Ṣuffah. He was among those concerning whom God’s words تعالى were revealed: “Nor is there blame upon those who, when they came to you that you might provide them mounts...” Both ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah and al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah also said, “I was the fourth person in Islam”; it is not known which of them preceded the other. He later settled in Homs. His hadith is in the four Sunan works. He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ and from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ. Those who narrated from him include Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀʾidh, Jubayr ibn Nufayr, Ḥujr ibn Ḥujr al-Kalāʿī, Saʿīd ibn Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī, Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bilāl, Abū Rahm al-Samāʿī, and several others. Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf said: He embraced Islam very early. Khalīfah said: He died during the civil strife of Ibn al-Zubayr. Abū Mushir said: He died after that, in the year seventy-five. In al-Ṭabarānī, by way of ʿUrwah ibn Ruwaym, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, who was a very old man among the Companions.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: براء ثم زاي وزن أحمد الكندي عداده في أهل الشام ذكره البخاري وابن السكن وغيرهما وقال بن حبان يقال إن له صحبة وروى بن منده من طريق محمد بن شعيب بن سابور عن يوسف بن سعيد عن عبد الملك بن أبي العباس الجذامي أبي عفيف عن عرزب الكندي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إنه سيحدث بعدي أشياء فأحبها أن تلزموا ما أحدث عمر قال محمد بن شعيب وأخبرني خلف بن أبي بديل عن أبي عفيف مثله وقال أبو حاتم الرازي عبد الملك أبو عفيف مجهول وشيخه لا يعرف
records.english: with rāʾ followed by zāy, on the pattern of Aḥmad, al-Kindī; counted among the people of Syria. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him, as did Ibn al-Sakan and others. Ibn Ḥibbān said: It is said that he had companionship. Ibn Mandah narrated by way of Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Sābūr, from Yūsuf ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās al-Judhāmī, Abū ʿAfīf, from ʿArzab al-Kindī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Things will happen after me, and the one I love most is that you adhere to what ʿUmar institutes.” Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb said: Khalaf ibn Abī Budayl also informed me, from Abū ʿAfīf, with the same. Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said: ʿAbd al-Malik Abū ʿAfīf is unknown, and his shaykh is not known.

names.arabic: عبد الملك بن أبي العباس الجذامي
names.english: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās al-Judhāmī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بضم أوله وسكون الراء بعدها مهملة بن عامر ويقال بن عمرو بن عامر بن ربيعة بن هوذة بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة العامري البكائي وفد هو وأخوه عروة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استدركه بن الدباغ وابن فتحون وروى بن قانع من طريق الزبير بن بكار عن ظمياء عن أبيها عبد العزيز عن جدها مولة عن ابني هوذة العرس وعروة ابني عمرو بن عامر البكائي أنهما وفدا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأقطعهما مسكنهما
records.english: with ḍammah on the first letter and quiescence on rāʾ, followed by unpointed sīn; ibn ʿĀmir, or ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah ibn Hawdhah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah, al-ʿĀmirī al-Bakkāʾī. He and his brother ʿUrwah came as a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Ibn al-Dabbāgh and Ibn Fatḥūn supplied his omission. Ibn Qāniʿ transmitted, by way of al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār, from Ẓamyāʾ, from her father ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from her grandfather Mawlah, from the two sons of Hawdhah, al-ʿUrs and ʿUrwah, the sons of ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir al-Bakkāʾī, that they came as a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he allotted them their dwelling place.

names.arabic: بن عمرو بن عامر بن ربيعة بن هوذة بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة
names.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah ibn Hawdhah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله الكندي أخو عدي أخرج حديثه أبو داود والنسائي وكأنه نزل الشام فإن حديثه عند أهلها وقد جاءت الرواية من طريق أخيه عدي بن عميرة عنه ومن طريقه عن أخيه عدي بن عميرة
records.english: with fatḥah on the first letter, al-Kindī, brother of ʿAdī; Abū Dāwūd transmitted his report, as did al-Nasāʾī. It appears that he settled in Syria, for his report is found among its people. The transmission has come by way of his brother ʿAdī ibn ʿUmayrah from him, and by way of him from his brother ʿAdī ibn ʿUmayrah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بن عبد البر فقال مذكور في الصحابة ولا أعرفه وقال أبو حاتم لأهل الشام عرسان عرس بن عميرة له صحبة وعرس بن قيس لا صحبة له وزعم العسكري أنهما واحد وأن عميرة أمه وقيسا أبوه وزعم بن قانع أن قيسا أبوه وعميرة جده فالله اعلم
records.english: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him and said, ‘He is mentioned among the Companions, but I do not know him.’ Abū Ḥātim said, ‘Among the people of Syria are two men named ʿArs: ʿArs ibn ʿUmayrah, who had companionship, and ʿArs ibn Qays, who had no companionship.’ Al-ʿAskarī claimed that they were one person, that ʿUmayrah was his mother, and that Qays was his father. Ibn Qāniʿ claimed that Qays was his father and ʿUmayrah his grandfather. فالله اعلم.

names.arabic: عرس بن قيس بن سعيد بن الأرقم بن النعمان الكندي
names.english: ʿArs ibn Qays ibn Saʿīd ibn al-Arqam ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Kindī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: عرس بن قيس بن سعيد بن الأرقم بن النعمان الكندي
title.english: ʿArs ibn Qays ibn Saʿīd ibn al-Arqam ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Kindī

records.arabic: بفتح أوله والفاء بينهما راء ساكنة وبالجيم بن اسعد بن كرب بن صفوان التميمي السعدي وقيل العطاردي كان من الفرسان في الجاهلية وشهد الكلاب فأصيب أنفه ثم أسلم فأذن له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يتخذ أنفا من ذهب أخرج حديثه أبو نعيم وهو معدود في أهل البصرة
records.english: with fatḥah on the first letter and fāʾ, with quiescent rāʾ between them, followed by jīm; ibn Asʿad ibn Karib ibn Ṣafwān al-Tamīmī al-Saʿdī, also said to be al-ʿUṭāridī. He was one of the horsemen in the pre-Islamic period and was present at al-Kulāb, where his nose was injured. He then embraced Islam, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم permitted him to fashion a nose of gold. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted his report. He is counted among the people of Basra.

names.arabic: بن اسعد بن كرب بن صفوان التميمي السعدي
names.english: ibn Asʿad ibn Karib ibn Ṣafwān al-Tamīmī al-Saʿdī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: وقيل بن صريح بالصاد المهملة أو المعجمة وقيل بن شريك وقيل بن شراحيل وقيل بن ذريح الأشجعي نزل الكوفة وحديثه عند مسلم وأبي داود والنسائي سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من خرج من أمتي وهم جميع على رجل يريد أن يشق عصاكم ويفرق جماعتكم وروى عن أبي بكر الصديق وعنه زياد بن علاقة وأبو حازم الأشجعي وأبو يعقوب العبدي وغيرهم
records.english: or ibn Ṣurayḥ with unpointed or pointed ṣād, or ibn Sharīk, or ibn Sharāḥīl, or ibn Dharīḥ, al-Ashjaʿī. He settled in Kufa. His report is found with Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Nasāʾī: ‘I heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “Whoever comes forth from my community while they are united under one man, intending to split your staff and divide your community.”’ He narrated from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and Ziyād ibn ʿAlāqah, Abū Ḥāzim al-Ashjaʿī, Abū Yaʿqūb al-ʿAbdī, and others narrated from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: فرق بن أبي خيثمة بينه وبين الأشجعي وقال البخاري هما واحد روى أبو عون الثقفي عن عرفجة السلمي عن أبي بكر الصديق حديثا فما أدري أهو هذا أو غيره
records.english: Ibn Abī Khaythamah distinguished him from the Ashjaʿī and said that al-Bukhārī regarded them as one person. Abū ʿAwn al-Thaqafī narrated from ʿArfajah al-Sulamī, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, a report; I do not know whether he is this man or someone else.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أحد الأمراء في الفتوح وقد تقدم أنهم كانوا لا يؤمرون إلا الصحابة وذكر وثيمة في الردة أن أبا بكر الصديق أمد به جيفر بن الجلندي لما ارتد أهلها وروى عن سهيل بن يوسف عن القاسم بن محمد أن أبا بكر الصديق أمره في حرب أهل الردة وقال بن دريد في الأخبار المنثورة حدثنا أبو حاتم عن أبي عبيدة قال أوصى عمر عتبة بن غزوان فقال فيها وقد أمرت العلاء بن الحضرمي أن يمدك بعرفجة بن هرثمة فإنه ذو مجاهدة ونكاية في العدو وكذا ذكر بن الكلبي وذكر سيف في الفتوح أن عمر كتب إلى سعد بن أبي وقاص أن سرح على الخيل عرفجة بن هرثمة فذكر القصة في فتح الموصل وتكريت وقال أبو زكريا المعافى الموصلي في تاريخ الموصل حدثني أبو غسان عن أبي عبيدة قال الذي جند الموصل عثمان وأسكنها أربعة آلاف وكان أمر عرفجة بن هرثمة فقطع بهم من فارس إلى الموصل
records.english: one of the commanders in the conquests. It has already been stated that they used to appoint only Companions as commanders. Wathīmah mentioned in his account of the apostasy that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq reinforced Jayfar ibn al-Julundā with him when the people there apostatized. He also related, from Suhayl ibn Yūsuf, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq appointed him as commander in the war against the apostates. Ibn Durayd said in al-Akhbār al-Manthūrah: Abū Ḥātim narrated to us from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said that ʿUmar gave instructions to ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān and said therein, ‘I have ordered al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī to reinforce you with ʿArfajah ibn Harthamah, for he is a man of striving and of inflicting harm upon the enemy.’ Ibn al-Kalbī likewise mentioned this. Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that ʿUmar wrote to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, ‘Dispatch ʿArfajah ibn Harthamah at the head of the cavalry,’ and he related the account of the conquest of Mosul and Tikrit. Abū Zakariyyā al-Muʿāfā al-Mawṣilī said in Tārīkh al-Mawṣil: Abū Ghassān narrated to me from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said, ‘The one who established Mosul as a garrison was ʿUthmān. He settled four thousand men there, and he had appointed ʿArfajah ibn Harthamah, who crossed with them from Persia to Mosul.’

names.arabic: عرفجة بن هرثمة بن عبد العزي بن زهير البارقي
names.english: ʿArfajah ibn Harthamah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Zuhayr al-Bāriqī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: عرفجة بن هرثمة بن عبد العزي بن زهير البارقي
title.english: ʿArfajah ibn Harthamah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Zuhayr al-Bāriqī

records.arabic: قال بن حبان يقال إن له صحبة وقال أبو موسى ذكره جعفر في الصحابة ولم يورد له شيئا
records.english: Ibn Ḥibbān said he was said to have companionship, and Abū Mūsā said that Jaʿfar mentioned him among the Companions but cited nothing concerning him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بضم أوله والفاء ويقال عرفجة الأنصاري تقدم ذكره في ترجمة أوس بن ثابت الأنصاري
records.english: with ḍammah on the first letter and fāʾ; also called ʿArfajah al-Anṣārī. He was mentioned earlier in the biography of Aws ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: حليف بن أمية والد أوفى استشهد بالطائف وضبط بن إسحاق أباه بجيم ونون وابن هشام بمهملة مضمومة بعدها موحدة وهو قول موسى بن عقبة
records.english: an ally of Ibn Umayyah and father of Awfā; he was martyred at Ṭāʾif. Ibn Isḥāq recorded his father’s name with jīm and nūn, while Ibn Hishām recorded it with a ḍammah-marked unpointed letter followed by bāʾ; this is also the view of Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: من بني نجاح ذكره الخرائطي في الهواتف وأورد عن أبي البختري وهب بن وهب القاضي المشهور بالضعف الشديد قال حدثني محمد بن إسحاق عن يحيى بن عبد الله بن الحارث عن أبيه عن جده عن سلمان الفارسي قال كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسجده في يوم مطير فسمعنا صوت السلام عليكم يا رسول الله فرد عليه فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أنت قال أنا عرفطة أتيتك مسلما وانتسب له كما ذكرنا فقال مرحبا بك أظهر لنا في صورتك قال سلمان فظهر لنا شيخ أرث أشعر وإذا بوجهه شعر غليظ متكاثف وإذا عيناه مشقوقتان طولا وله فم في صدره أنياب بادية طوال وإذا في أصابعه أظفار مخاليب كأنياب السباع فاقشعرت منه جلودنا فقال الشيخ يا نبي الله أرسل معي من يدعو جماعة من قومي إلى الإسلام وأنا أرده إليك سالما فذكر قصة طويلة في بعثه معه علي بن أبي طالب فأركبه على بعير وأردفه سلمان وأنهم نزلوا في واد لا زرع فيه ولا شجر وأن عليا أكثر من ذكر الله ثم صلى سلمان بالشيخ الصبح ثم قام خطيبا فتذمروا عليه فدعا بدعاء طويل فنزلت صواعق أحرقت كثيرا ثم أذعن من بقي وأقروا بالإسلام ورجع بعلي وسلمان فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي لما قص قصتهم أما إنهم لا يزالون لك هائبين إلى يوم القيامة
records.english: from Banū Najāḥ; al-Kharāʾiṭī mentioned him in al-Hawātif and cited from Abū al-Bakhtarī Wahb ibn Wahb, the judge well known for his extreme weakness, who said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to me from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from his father, from his grandfather, from Salmān al-Fārisī, who said: We were with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in his mosque on a rainy day when we heard a voice say, ‘Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.’ He returned the greeting, and the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم asked him, ‘Who are you?’ He said, ‘I am ʿUrfuṭah. I have come to you as a Muslim,’ and he gave his lineage as we have mentioned. He said, ‘Welcome. Show yourself to us in your form.’ Salmān said: An unkempt, hairy old man appeared to us. His face had thick, dense hair, his eyes were slit lengthwise, he had a mouth in his chest with long, protruding canine teeth, and his fingers bore talons like the fangs of beasts. Our skins shuddered at him. The old man said, ‘O Prophet of God, send with me someone to call a group of my people to Islam, and I shall return him safely to you.’ He then related a long account of the Prophet’s sending ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib with him: he mounted him on a camel and placed Salmān behind him; they alighted in a valley with neither crops nor trees; ʿAlī repeatedly remembered God; then Salmān led the old man in the dawn prayer and afterward stood to address them. They grumbled against him, so he uttered a lengthy supplication, and thunderbolts descended and burned many of them. Those who remained then submitted and acknowledged Islam. He returned with ʿAlī and Salmān. When ʿAlī recounted their story, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said to him, ‘Indeed, they will continue to hold you in awe until the Day of Resurrection.’

names.arabic: يحيى بن عبد الله بن الحارث
names.english: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو مكعت يأتي في الكنى وله ذكر في ترجمة حضرمي بن عامر
records.english: or Mukʿat; he will appear under the kunyas and is mentioned in the biography of Ḥaḍramī ibn ʿĀmir.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح النون الهرمي قال بن عبد البر له صحبة قلت وحديثه عند أبي سعيد بن الأعرابي في معجمه في ترجمة الحسن بن أبي الربيع عن عبد الزراق بسند ضعيف إلى صفوان بن أمية قال كنا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقام عرفطة بن نهيك فقال يا رسول الله إني وأهل بيتي مرزوقون من هذا الصيد ولنا فيه قسم وبركة وهو مشغلة عن ذكر الله أفتحله أو تحرمه فقال لا بل أحله الحديث
records.english: with fatḥah on nūn, al-Haramī; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said he had companionship. I said: His report is found in the Muʿjam of Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Aʿrābī, in the biography of al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Rabīʿ, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, through a weak chain to Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah, who said: We were with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم when ʿUrfuṭah ibn Nuhayk stood and said, ‘O Messenger of God, my household and I receive our provision from this hunting, and in it we have an allotted share and blessing, but it distracts from the remembrance of God. Do you declare it lawful or forbidden?’ He said, ‘No; rather, I declare it lawful.’ The report continues.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ويقال بن أبي أثاثة بن عبد العزي بن حرثان بن عوف بن عبيد بن عويج بن عدي بن كعب القرشي العدوي من السابقين الأولين ممن هاجر إلى الحبشة عند موسى بن عقبة والجمهور سوى بن إسحاق وهو أخو عمرو بن العاص لأمه
records.english: also said to be ibn Abī Athāthah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ḥarthān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUwayj ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī. He was among the earliest forerunners who emigrated to Abyssinia, according to Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and the majority other than Ibn Isḥāq. He was the maternal brother of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

names.arabic: بن أبي أثاثة بن عبد العزي بن حرثان بن عوف بن عبيد بن عويج بن عدي بن كعب
names.english: ibn Abī Athāthah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ḥarthān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUwayj ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن حبيب بن حارثة بن هلال بن سماك بن عوف بن امرئ القيس بن بهثة بن سليم السلمي حليف بني عمرو بن عوف من الأنصار ذكره بن إسحاق وغيره فيمن استشهد ببئر معونة وثبت ذكره في غزوة الرجيع من صحيح البخاري من طريق أبي أسامة عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه فذكر القصة مرسلة وفي آخرها وكان فيهم يومئذ عروة بن أسماء بن الصلت فسمى عروة به أي بعد ذلك
records.english: ibn Ḥabīb ibn Ḥārithah ibn Hilāl ibn Simāk ibn ʿAwf ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Bahthah ibn Sulaym, al-Sulamī, an ally of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf of the Anṣār. Ibn Isḥāq and others mentioned him among those martyred at Biʾr Maʿūnah. His mention is established in the account of the expedition of al-Rajīʿ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, by way of Abū Usāmah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who related the account without a Companion in the chain. At its end is: ‘Among them that day was ʿUrwah ibn Asmāʾ ibn al-Ṣalt.’ ʿUrwah was named after him—that is, afterward.

names.arabic: بن حبيب بن حارثة بن هلال بن سماك بن عوف بن امرئ القيس بن بهثة بن سليم
names.english: ibn Ḥabīb ibn Ḥārithah ibn Hilāl ibn Simāk ibn ʿAwf ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Bahthah ibn Sulaym

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ويقال بن أبي الجعد وصوب الثاني بن المديني وقال بن قانع اسمه أبو الجعد البارقي وزعم الرشاطي أنه عروة بن عياض بن أبي الجعد وأنه نسب إلى جده مشهور وله أحاديث وهو الذي أرسله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليشتري الشاة بدينار فاشترى به شاتين والحديث مشهور في البخاري وغيره وكان فيمن حضر فتوح الشام ونزلها ثم سيرة عثمان إلى الكوفة وحديثه عند أهلها وقال شبيب بن غردقة رأيت في دار عروة بن الجعد ستين فرسا مربوطة
records.english: also said to be ibn Abī al-Jaʿd; Ibn al-Madīnī preferred the latter, and Ibn said Qāniʿ that his name was Abū al-Jaʿd al-Bāriqī. Al-Rushāṭī claimed that he was ʿUrwah ibn ʿIyāḍ ibn Abī al-Jaʿd and that he was ascribed to his grandfather. He is well known and has reports. He is the one whom the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent to buy a sheep for one dinar; he bought two sheep with it. The report is well known in al-Bukhārī and elsewhere. He was among those present at the conquests of Syria and settled there. The next words, thumma sīrata ʿUthmān ilā al-Kūfah, are damaged; who moved, who acted, and how ʿUthmān relates to the movement remain unresolved. His reports are found among the people of Kufa. Shabīb ibn Gharqadah said, ‘I saw sixty horses tethered in the house of ʿUrwah ibn al-Jaʿd.’

names.arabic: عروة بن عياض بن أبي الجعد
names.english: ʿUrwah ibn ʿIyāḍ ibn Abī al-Jaʿd

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
تقدم ذكر أبيه وهو صحابي مشهور وقد شهد مع أبيه بعض الحروب في الجاهلية فالظاهر أنه احتمع بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال المبرد في الكامل يروى عن حماد الرواية عن ليلى بنت عروة بن زيد الخيل قالت قلت لأبي أنشد قول أبيك
بني عامر هل تعرفون إذا غدا
أبا مكنف قد شد عقد الدوائر الأبيات هل شهدت هذه الغزاة مع أبيك قال نعم قلت بن كم كنت قال غلاما ورواها أبو الفرج من طريق حماد الرواية وزاد من وجه أنه عاش إلى خلافة علي وشهد معه صفين وأنشد المرزباني في شهوده القادسية في خلافة عمر شعرا يقول فيه
برزت لأهل القادسية معلما
وما كل من يغشى الكريهة يعلم وقال سيف في الفتوح
records.english: his father was mentioned earlier; he was a well-known Companion and took part with his father in some of the wars of the pre-Islamic period. The text then says that it appears he aḥtamaʿa with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم; the verb is corrupt, so the proposed encounter remains unresolved. Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kāmil: It is narrated from Ḥammād al-Rāwiyah, from Laylā bint ʿUrwah ibn Zayd al-Khayl, that she said, ‘I said to my father: Recite the words of your father: “Banū ʿĀmir, do you recognize, when he set forth at dawn, / Abū Miknaf, who had firmly tied the knots of the circuits...”’ and the ensuing verses. ‘Were you present with your father on this expedition?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I asked, ‘How old were you?’ He said, ‘A boy.’ Abū al-Faraj narrated it by way of Ḥammād al-Rāwiyah and added, by another route, that he lived until the caliphate of ʿAlī and was present with him at Ṣiffīn. Al-Marzubānī cited, concerning his presence at al-Qādisiyyah during the caliphate of ʿUmar, poetry in which he said: ‘I came forth against the people of al-Qādisiyyah, marked for recognition; / not everyone who plunges into hardship is so marked.’ Sayf said in al-Futūḥ [the source ends here].

names.arabic: ليلى بنت عروة بن زيد الخيل
names.english: Laylā bint ʿUrwah ibn Zayd al-Khayl

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: وقيل الجهني مختلف في صحبته قال الباوردي له صحبة أخرج حديثه أحمد ووقع في روايته القرشي وابن شاهين ووقع في روايته الجهني وبذلك جزم العسكري وأخرجه أبو داود أيضا كلهم من طريق حبيب بن أبي ثابت عن عروة بن عامر قال ذكرت الطيرة عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أحسنها الفأل ولا ترد مسلما الحديث رجاله ثقات دون المراسيل لكن حبيب كثير الإرسال وأخرج أبو داود له في السنن ما يشعر بأنه عنده صحابي وقد جزم أبو أحمد العسكري بأن رواية عروة هذه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلة وكذلك البيهقي في الدعاء وقال بن المبارك في الزهد أنبأنا سفيان بن حبيب بن ثابت عن عروة بن عامر قال تعرض عليه ذنوبه يوم القيامة فيمر بالذنب من ذنوبه فيقول أما إني كنت منك مشفقا فيغفر له ومثل هذا لا يقال بالرأي فيكون في حكم المرفوع واستدل أبو موسى على ذلك بقول أبي حاتم عروة بن عامر روى عن بن عباس وعبيدة بن رفاعة روى عنه حبيب بن أبي ثابت وليست دلالة ذلك بواضحة فلا يلزم من كونه يروى عن الصحابة بل التابعين ألا يكون صحابيا نعم قال بن أبي حاتم في المراسيل أخرج أبي حديث عروة بن عامر في الوحدان أي من الصحابة ثم بين علته فالله أعلم وبين البخاري أن الاختلاف في نسبه عن الأعمش
records.english: also said to be al-Juhanī; his companionship is disputed. Al-Bāwardī said he had companionship. Aḥmad transmitted his report, in whose version he is called al-Qurashī, as did Ibn Shāhīn, in whose version he is called al-Juhanī; al-ʿAskarī asserted the latter. Abū Dāwūd also transmitted it. All of them did so by way of Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir, who said: Omens were mentioned in the presence of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he said, ‘The best of them is a good sign, and it does not turn a Muslim back.’ The report continues. Its transmitters are trustworthy apart from the issue of disconnected reports, but Ḥabīb transmitted many disconnected reports. Abū Dāwūd transmitted material from him in al-Sunan which suggests that he regarded him as a Companion. Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAskarī asserted that this narration of ʿUrwah from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم is disconnected, as did al-Bayhaqī in al-Duʿāʾ. Ibn al-Mubārak said in al-Zuhd: Sufyān informed us from Ḥabīb ibn Thābit, from ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir, who said, ‘His sins will be displayed to him on the Day of Resurrection. He will pass by one of his sins and say, “Indeed, I used to be fearful of you,” and he will be forgiven.’ Something like this is not said on the basis of personal opinion, so it has the ruling of a report traced to the Prophet. Abū Mūsā inferred this from Abū Ḥātim’s statement: ‘ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUbaydah ibn Rifāʿah, and Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit narrated from him.’ The indication is not clear. His narrating from Companions—and indeed from Successors—does not necessarily mean that he was not himself a Companion. Ibn Abī Ḥātim did, however, say in al-Marāsīl: ‘My father included the report of ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir in al-Wuḥdān’—that is, among the Companions—then explained its defect. فالله أعلم. Al-Bukhārī explained that the variation in his lineage came from al-Aʿmash.

records.arabic:
قال بن حبان له صحبة وتبعه المستغفري وأورده أبو موسى بذلك ولم يورد له شيئا قال محمد بن سعد والباوردي عروة الأسلمي شهد صفين مع علي كذلك عده عبيد الله بن أبي رافع في الصحابة الذين شهدوا صفين ويقال إنه الذي عناه علي بن أبي طالب بقوله
جزى الله خيرا عصبة أسلمية
حسان الوجوه صرعوا حول هاشم
يزيد وعبد الله منهم ومعبد
وعروة وابنا مالك في الأكارم
records.english: Ibn Ḥibbān said he had companionship, and al-Mustaghfirī followed him and included him on that basis. Abū Mūsā likewise included him but cited nothing concerning him. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd and al-Bāwardī said that ʿUrwah al-Aslamī was present at Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ likewise counted him among the Companions who were present at Ṣiffīn. It is said that he is the one whom ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib meant in his words: ‘May God reward well a band of Aslamīs, / handsome of face, who fell around Hāshim: / Yazīd and ʿAbd Allāh among them, and Maʿbad, / and ʿUrwah and the two sons of Mālik, among the noble.’

records.arabic: بالمهملة والمثناة المشددة بن مالك بن كعب بن عمرو بن سعد بن عوف بن ثقيف الثقفي وهو عم والد المغيرة بن شعبة وأمه سبيعة بنت عبد شمس بن عبد مناف أخت آمنة كان أحد الأكابر من قومه وقيل إنه المراد بقوله على رجل من القريتين عظيم قال بن عباس وعكرمة ومحمد بن كعب وقتادة والسدي المراد بالقريتين مكة والمدينة واختلفوا في تعيين الرجل المراد فعن قتادة أرادوا الوليد بن المغيرة من أهل مكة وعروة بن مسعود الثقفي من أهل الطائف وعن مجاهد عتبة بن ربيعة وعمير بن عروة بن مسعود وعنه رواية بن عبد ياليل بدل حبيب وعن السدي الوليد وكنانة بن عبد عمرو بن عمير وعن بن عباس الوليد وحبيب بن عمرو بن عمير الثقفي وثبت ذكر عروة بن مسعود في الحديث الصحيح في قصة الحديبية وكانت له اليد البيضاء في تقرير الصلح وهو مستوفى في البخاري وترجمة بن عبد البر بأنه شهد الحديبة وهو كذلك لكن في العرف إذا أطلق على الصحابي أنه شهد غزوة كذا يتبادر أن المراد أنه شهدها مسلما فلا يقال شهد معاوية بدرا لأنه لو أطلق ذلك ظن من لا خبرة له لكونه عرف أنه صحابي أنه شهدها مع المسلمين وعند مسلم من حديث جابر مرفوعا عرض على الأنبياء فذكر الحديث قال ورأيت عيسى فإذا أقرب من رأيت به شبها عروة بن مسعود وذكر موسى بن عتبة عن بن شهاب وأبو الأسود عن عروة وكذلك ذكره بن إسحاق يزيد بعضهم على بعض أن أبا بكر لما صدر من الحج سنة تسع قدم عروة بن مسعود الثقفي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي رواية بن إسحاق أنه اتبع أثر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما انصرف من الطائف فأسلم واستأذن أن يرجع إلى قومه فقال إني أخاف أن يقتلوك قال لو وجدوني نائما ما أيقظوني فأذن له فدعاهم إلى الإسلام ونصح لهم فعصوه وأسمعوه من الأذى فلما كان من السحر قام على غرفة له فأذن فرماه رجل من ثقيف بسهم فقتله فلما بلغ ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال مثل عروة مثل صاحب ياسين دعا قومه إلى الله فقتلوه واختلف في اسم قاتله فقيل أوس بن عوف وقيل وهب بن جابر وقيل لعروة ما ترى في دمك قال كرامة أكرمني الله بها وشهادة ساقها الله إلى فليس في إلا ما في الشهداء الذين قتلوا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يرتحل عنكم فادفنوني معهم فدفنوه معهم وروى أبو نعيم من طريق داود بن عاصم عن عروة بن مسعود وهو جده كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوضع عنده الماء فإذا بايع النساء يمس أيديهن فيه وهذا منقطع وفي الإسناد إلى داود ضعف أيضا وروى بن منده من طريق إبراهيم بن محمد بن عاصم عن أبيه عن حذيفة عن عروة بن مسعود الثقفي قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لقنوا موتاكم لا إله إلا الله فإنها تهدم الخطايا إسناده ضعيف أيضا أورده العقيلي في ترجمة إبراهيم بن محمد بن عاصم ولكن أر فيه الثقفي
records.english: with unpointed ʿayn and doubled tāʾ, ibn Mālik ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAwf ibn Thaqīf, al-Thaqafī. He was the paternal uncle of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah’s father. His mother was Subayʿah bint ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf, the sister of Āminah. He was one of the leading men of his people. It is said that he is the one intended by the words, ‘to a great man from the two towns.’ Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatādah, and al-Suddī said that the two towns meant were Mecca and Medina, but they differed in identifying the man intended. According to Qatādah, they meant al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah of Mecca and ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī of Ṭāʾif. According to Mujāhid, they were ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah and ʿUmayr ibn ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd; in another narration from him, Ibn ʿAbd Yālīl appears in place of Ḥabīb. According to al-Suddī, they were al-Walīd and Kinānah ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr. According to Ibn ʿAbbās, they were al-Walīd and Ḥabīb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr al-Thaqafī. ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd is established in the sound report concerning the story of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and he rendered distinguished service in arranging the truce. The account appears in full in al-Bukhārī. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr headed his biography by saying that he was present at al-Ḥudaybiyyah, which is correct. In customary usage, however, when it is said without qualification that a Companion was present at a particular expedition, it is understood that he was present as a Muslim. One would therefore not say that Muʿāwiyah was present at Badr, because an uninformed person who knew that he was a Companion might suppose that he was present with the Muslims. In Muslim, in a report traced to the Prophet from Jābir, is: ‘The prophets were shown to me’—and he related the report—‘and I saw Jesus; the person I have seen who most closely resembles him is ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd.’ Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah mentioned from Ibn Shihāb, and Abū al-Aswad from ʿUrwah—as did Ibn Isḥāq, each adding to the account of the others—that when Abū Bakr returned from the pilgrimage in the ninth year, ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. In Ibn Isḥāq’s version, he followed the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم after he departed from Ṭāʾif, embraced Islam, and asked permission to return to his people. He said, ‘I fear that they will kill you.’ ʿUrwah replied, ‘If they found me asleep, they would not wake me.’ He gave him permission. ʿUrwah called them to Islam and counseled them. They disobeyed him and made him hear abuse. At dawn he stood in an upper room and gave the call to prayer. A man of Thaqīf shot him with an arrow and killed him. When the news reached the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, he said, ‘The likeness of ʿUrwah is the likeness of the companion of Yā Sīn: he called his people to God, and they killed him.’ There is disagreement over the name of his killer: it is said to have been Aws ibn ʿAwf, and it is said to have been Wahb ibn Jābir. ʿUrwah was asked, ‘What do you think of your blood?’ He said, ‘It is an honor with which God has honored me and a martyrdom God has brought to me. There is nothing in me except what was in the martyrs who were killed with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم before he departed from among you. Bury me with them.’ They buried him with them. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted, by way of Dāwūd ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd—who was his grandfather—that water would be placed before the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, and when he accepted the women’s pledge, he would touch their hands in it. This report is disconnected, and the chain to Dāwūd is also weak. Ibn Mandah transmitted, by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĀṣim, from his father, from Ḥudhayfah, from ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, who said that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم used to say, ‘Prompt your dying to say, “There is no god but God,” for it demolishes sins.’ Its chain is also weak. Al-ʿUqaylī cited it in the biography of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĀṣim, but I see ‘al-Thaqafī’ in it.

records.arabic: بمعجمة وآخره مهملة وتشديد الراء بن أوس بن حارثة بن لام بن عمرو بن طريف بن عمرو بن عامر الطائي كان من بيت الرياسة في قومه وجده كان سيدهم وكذا أبوه وهذا كان يباري عدي بن حاتم في الرياسة ووقع حديثه في السنن الأربعة وسنن الدارقطني من طريق الشعبي عن عروة بن مضرس قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمزدلفة فقلت يا رسول الله إنني أكللت راحلتي وأتعبت نفسي فهل لي من حج الحديث وقال الدارقطني في الإلزامات لم يرو عنه غير الشعبي وسبقه إلى ذلك علي بن المديني ومسلم وغير واحد وقال الأزدي روى عنه أيضا حميد بن منهب ولا يقوم وروى الحاكم من طريق عروة بن الزبير عن عروة بن مضرس حديثا لكن إسناده ضعيف وذكر أبو صالح المؤذن أنه روى عنه بن عباس أيضا وقال بن سعد كان عروة مع خالد بن الوليد حين بعثه أبو بكر على الردة قال وهو الذي بعث خالد معه عيينة بن حصن إلى أبي بكر لما أسره يوم البطاح
records.english: with pointed ḍād and ending in unpointed sīn, with doubled rāʾ; ibn Aws ibn Ḥārithah ibn Lām ibn ʿAmr ibn Ṭarīf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir al-Ṭāʾī. He belonged to the leading house among his people. His grandfather was their chief, as was his father, and he vied with ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim for leadership. His report appears in the four Sunan collections and in Sunan al-Dāraquṭnī, by way of al-Shaʿbī, from ʿUrwah ibn Muḍarris, who said: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم at Muzdalifah and said, ‘O Messenger of God, I have exhausted my mount and wearied myself. Have I attained the pilgrimage?’ The report continues. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in al-Ilzāmāt that no one other than al-Shaʿbī narrated from him. ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, Muslim, and more than one other scholar had already said the same. Al-Azdī said that Ḥumayd ibn Manhab also narrated from him, but this is not established. Al-Ḥākim transmitted by way of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿUrwah ibn Muḍarris, a report, but its chain is weak. Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Muʾadhdhin mentioned that Ibn ʿAbbās also narrated from him. Ibn Saʿd said that ʿUrwah was with Khālid ibn al-Walīd when Abū Bakr sent him against the apostates. He said that ʿUrwah was the one with whom Khālid sent ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn to Abū Bakr after taking him captive on the day of al-Biṭāḥ.

names.arabic: بن عمرو بن طريف بن عمرو بن عامر الطائي

records.arabic: قال البغوي سكن الشام ذكره محمد بن إسماعيل وقال له حديث لم يذكره قلت وذكره الحسن بن أبي سفيان وابن أبي خيثمة وابن قانع والإسماعيلي في الصحابة ورووه كلهم من طريق إسماعيل بن عياش عن عتبة بن تميم عن الوليد بن عامر عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قضى أن صاحب الدابة أحق بصدرها وأخرجه أبو زرعة في مسند الشاميين ويعقوب بن سفيان في تاريخه والدارقطني في المؤتلف فقالوا عن عروة عن عمر بن الخطاب والاختلاف فيه على إسماعيل فرواه عن هشام بن عمار كالأول ورواه أبو اليمان عنه كالثاني وقد حكى بن ماكولا الخلاف في أبيه هل هو بالمعجمة والمثلثة آخره أو بالمهملة وآخره موحدة وتبع في ذلك الخطيب فقد أخرجه في المؤتلف بالوجهين
records.english: al-Baghawī said he settled in Syria; Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl mentioned him and said that he had a report, which he did not cite. I said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Sufyān, Ibn Abī Khaythamah, Ibn Qāniʿ, and al-Ismāʿīlī mentioned him among the Companions. All of them transmitted, by way of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿUtbah ibn Tamīm, from al-Walīd ibn ʿĀmir, from him, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم ruled that the owner of a riding animal has the greater right to its forepart. Abū Zurʿah transmitted it in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn, as did Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān in his Tārīkh and al-Dāraquṭnī in al-Muʾtalif; they said: from ʿUrwah, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. The variation concerning it is attributable to Ismāʿīl. Hishām ibn ʿAmmār narrated it from him according to the first version, while Abū al-Yamān narrated it from him according to the second. Ibn Mākūlā related the disagreement over his father’s name: whether it is written with a pointed letter and ends in thāʾ, or with an unpointed letter and ends in bāʾ. He followed al-Khaṭīb in this, for al-Khaṭīb transmitted it in al-Muʾtalif in both forms.

records.english: his kunya was Abū Salāmah; he will appear under the kunyas.

records.arabic: بفاء ثم قاف مصغرا يكنى أبا غاضرة قال بن حبان يقال إن له صحبة وقال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه له صحبة وروى حديثه عاصم بن هلال عن غاضرة بن عروة الفقيمي أخبرني أبي قال أتيت المدينة فدخلت المسجد فلما صلينا جعل الناس يقولون يا رسول الله أرأيت كذا أرأيت كذا فقال يا أيها الناس إن دين الله يسر الحديث رواه أحمد والبغوي وأبو يعلى وغيرهم وعاصم مختلف في الاحتجاج به وقال الدارقطني إنه تفرد به
records.english: with fāʾ followed by qāf, in the diminutive; his kunya was Abū Ghāḍirah. Ibn Ḥibbān said he was said to have companionship. Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from his father that he had companionship. ʿĀṣim ibn Hilāl narrated his report from Ghāḍirah ibn ʿUrwah al-Fuqaymī: ‘My father informed me, saying: I came to Medina and entered the mosque. After we prayed, the people began saying, “O Messenger of God, what do you say about such and such? What do you say about such and such?” He said, “O people, God’s religion is ease.”’ The report continues. Aḥmad, al-Baghawī, Abū Yaʿlā, and others transmitted it. There is disagreement over whether ʿĀṣim may be relied upon as proof, and al-Dāraquṭnī said that he alone transmitted it.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى الإسماعيلي من طريق عبد السلام بن حرب عن كلثوم بن زياد عمن ذكره عن عروة القشيري قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال قد أفلح من رزق لنا الحديث أورده أبو موسى فقال قد روى هذا القول عن غير هذا الرجل
records.english: al-Ismāʿīlī transmitted through ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb from Kulthūm ibn Ziyād, from someone he mentioned, from ʿUrwah al-Qushayrī, who said: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he said, ‘He has prospered who was granted—lanā.’ The report continues; lanā is damaged here, and the object or complement after ‘was granted’ remains unresolved. Abū Mūsā cited it and said, ‘This statement has also been narrated from a man other than this one.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي فقال قال محمد بن إسماعيل له حديث ولم يذكره وذكره المستغفري وأبو موسى
records.english: al-Baghawī mentioned him and said Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said he had a report, but did not cite it. Al-Mustaghfirī and Abū Mūsā also mentioned him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله بن زيد النهدي ذكره الهمداني في الأنساب وقال وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع أبي شمر بن أبرهة حكاه الرشاطي وقال ولم يذكره بن عبد البر ولا بن فتحون
records.english: with fatḥah on the first letter, ibn Zayd al-Nahdī; al-Hamdānī mentioned him in al-Ansāb and said he came in a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with Abū Shamir ibn Abrahah. Al-Rushāṭī related this and said, ‘Neither Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr nor Ibn Fatḥūn mentioned him.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أبو عبد الله عداده في أهل الشام قال البخاري له صحبة وقال بن أبي حاتم إسناده ليس بالقائم وقال بن حبان يقال له صحبة وقال بن السكن يقال إنه كان راعيا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى الطبراني من طريق يزيد بن عبد الله بن عريب عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الخيل معقود في نواصيها الخير إلى يوم القيامة وروى بقية عن عبد الله بن عريب عن أبيه عن جده حديثا رفعه لن يخبل الشيطان أحدا في داره فرس عتيق أخرجه بن منده من طريق أبي عتبة عن بقية وأظنه سقط منه رجل لكن روى بن قانع من طريق سعيد بن سنان عن عمرو بن عريب عن أبيه عن جده هذا الحديث بعينه وهذا اختلاف شديد وعريب بمهملة بوزن عظيم
records.english: Abū ʿAbd Allāh, counted among the people of Syria. Al-Bukhārī said he had companionship. Ibn Abī Ḥātim said that his chain of transmission was not sound. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he was said to have companionship. Ibn al-Sakan said that he was said to have been a shepherd for the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted, by way of Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿArīb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, ‘Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection.’ Baqiyyah narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿArīb, from his father, from his grandfather, a report that he traced to the Prophet: ‘Satan will never derange anyone in whose house there is a pedigreed horse.’ Ibn Mandah transmitted it by way of Abū ʿUtbah, from Baqiyyah. I think one man has dropped out of its chain. Ibn Qāniʿ, however, transmitted this very report by way of Saʿīd ibn Sinān, from ʿAmr ibn ʿArīb, from his father, from his grandfather. This is a severe variation. ʿArīb is written with an unpointed letter and follows the pattern of ʿAẓīm.

names.arabic: يزيد بن عبد الله بن عريب
names.english: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿArīb

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بالتصغير بن مالك الأسلمي قرأته بخط بن فطيس مضبوطا وقيل إنه اسم ماعز بن مالك الذي رجم وأن ماعزا كان لقبه
records.english: in the diminutive, ibn Mālik al-Aslamī; I read it with its vocalization in Ibn Faṭīs's handwriting. It is said that this was the name of Māʿiz ibn Mālik, who was stoned, and that Māʿiz was his nickname.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له صحبة ذكره بن سعد
records.english: he had companionship; Ibn Saʿd mentioned him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الطبري في الصحابة من طريق العوام بن حوشب عن عزرة بن الحارث قال كنا إذ صلينا خلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرفعنا رؤوسنا قمنا فإذا سجد اتبعناه
records.english: al-Ṭabarī listed him among the Companions through al-ʿAwwām ibn Ḥawshab from ʿAzrah ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: When we prayed behind the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, we raised our heads and stood; when he prostrated, we followed him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكر الواقدي أنه وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو وأخوه فروة بن مالك فأسلما واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: al-Wāqidī mentioned that he and his brother Farwah ibn Mālik came in a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. They embraced Islam. Ibn Fatḥūn supplied his omission.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بفتح أوله بن أبي سبرة تقدم فيمن اسمه عبد الرحمن قال المرزباني هاجر سبرة وعزيز ابنا يزيد بن مالك بن عبيد بن ذؤيب الجعفي فلحق بهما أبوهما فقال
وسبرة كان النفس لو أن حاجة
ترد ولكن كان أمرا وأنفرا
وكان عزيز خلتي فرأيته
تولى فلم يقبل علي وأدبرا فوفدوا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسلموا وحسن إسلامهم
records.english: with fatḥah on the first letter, ibn Abī Sabrah; he appeared earlier among those named ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: Al-Marzubānī related that Sabrah and ʿAzīz, the two sons of Yazīd ibn Mālik ibn ʿUbayd ibn Dhuʾayb al-Juʿfī, emigrated. Their father followed them and said: ‘Sabrah was as my very soul—if any need could have turned him back— / but it was a matter that made him flee. / ʿAzīz was my intimate friend, yet I saw him / turn away, neither facing me nor drawing near.’ They came in a delegation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, embraced Islam, and practiced Islam well.

names.arabic: يزيد بن مالك بن عبيد بن ذؤيب الجعفي
names.english: Yazīd ibn Mālik ibn ʿUbayd ibn Dhuʾayb al-Juʿfī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بضم أوله وتشديد المهملة العذري ذكره بن أبي حاتم وقال له صحبة وروى من طريق زياد بن نصر عن سليم بن مطير عن أبيه عن عس العذري أنه استقطع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أرضا بوادي القرى فأقطعه إياها فهي إلى اليوم تسمى بويرة عس وقال رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غزا تبوك فصلى في مسجد وادي القرى وأخرجه بن منده من هذا الوجه وقال بن الجارود اختلف في اسمه وعس أصح وذكره البرديجي في الأسماء المفردة لكنه ضبطه بالشين المعجمة وكذا ذكره بن ماكولا يقال هو شاعر جاهلي وهو عش بن لبيد بن عداء بن أمية بن عبد الله بن رزاح من بني عذرة وظاهر صنيعه أنه غير الصحابي فعند المستغفري أنه عثير بمثلثة مصغرا وعند غيره أنه بالمثناة كذلك تقدم في عريب والراجح أنه غير هذا كما أشرت إليه هناك وعند عبد الغني أنه بفتح أوله وسكون النون بعدها مثناة وعند بن عبد البر أنه بنون وزاي مصغرا والله أعلم
records.english: with ḍammah on the first letter and doubled unpointed sīn, al-ʿUdhrī. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him and said he had companionship. He transmitted, by way of Ziyād ibn Naṣr, from Sulaym ibn Muṭayr, from his father, from ʿUss al-ʿUdhrī, that he asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم to allot him land in Wādī al-Qurā, and he allotted it to him. To this day it is called Buwayrat ʿUss. He said, ‘I saw the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم when he campaigned at Tabūk, and he prayed in the mosque of Wādī al-Qurā.’ Ibn Mandah transmitted it by this route. Ibn al-Jārūd said there was disagreement over his name and that ʿUss was the soundest form. Al-Bardījī mentioned him among the unique names but recorded it with pointed shīn. Ibn Mākūlā likewise mentioned him, saying that he was a pre-Islamic poet: ʿUshsh ibn Labīd ibn ʿAddāʾ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Razāḥ of Banū ʿUdhrah. The apparent sense of his treatment is that this person was not the Companion. According to al-Mustaghfirī, the name is ʿUthayr, with thāʾ, in the diminutive; according to another scholar it likewise has tāʾ. He appeared earlier under ʿArīb. The more likely view is that he is someone other than this man, as I indicated there. According to ʿAbd al-Ghanī, its first letter has fatḥah and is followed by quiescent nūn and then tāʾ. According to Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, it has nūn and zāy and is in the diminutive. والله أعلم.

names.arabic: عش بن لبيد بن عداء بن أمية بن عبد الله بن رزاح
names.english: ʿUshsh ibn Labīd ibn ʿAddāʾ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Razāḥ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
أبو صفرة التميمي البصري له ذكر في الصحيح في حديث الجندب وذكره بن أبي حاتم بين صحابيين في الأفراد من حرف العين ولم يفصح البخاري بشيء بل رسم الترجمة وقال نسبه شعبة عن الأزرق وكذا صنع مسلم وقال بن منده ذكر في الصحابة ولا يثبت وقال بن عبد البر يقولون إن حديثه مرسل وبذلك جزم العسكري وابن حبان وقد روى حديثه أبو داود الطيالسي عن شعبة عن الأزرق عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال صبر ساعة في بعض المواطن خير من عبادة أربعين عاما الحديث وله حديث آخر أخرجه الدارقطني وقال بن المبارك في الزهد أنبأنا محمد بن ثابت العبدي حدثنا هارون بن رئاب سمعت عسعس بن سلامة يقول لأصحابه سأحدثكم ببيت من شعر فتعجبوا فقال
إن تنج منها تنج من ذي عظيمة
وإلا فإني لا إخالك ماضيا أي إن تنج من مسألة القبر فأخذ القوم يبكون بكاء ما رأيتهم بكوا من شيء ما بكوا يومئذ
records.english: Abū Ṣafrah al-Tamīmī al-Baṣrī; he is mentioned in al-Ṣaḥīḥ in the report of Jundub. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him between two Companions among the unique names beginning with ʿayn. Al-Bukhārī made no explicit statement; rather, he merely entered the biographical heading and said, ‘Shuʿbah gave his lineage from al-Azraq.’ Muslim did the same. Ibn Mandah said, ‘He is mentioned among the Companions, but that is not established.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that they regarded his report as disconnected; al-ʿAskarī and Ibn Ḥibbān stated this definitively. Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī transmitted his report from Shuʿbah, from al-Azraq, from him, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, ‘Steadfastness for an hour in certain situations is better than forty years of worship.’ The report continues. He has another report transmitted by al-Dāraquṭnī. Ibn al-Mubārak said in al-Zuhd: Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-ʿAbdī informed us; Hārūn ibn Riʾāb narrated to us: I heard ʿAsʿas ibn Salāmah say to his companions, ‘I will tell you a line of poetry,’ and they were surprised. He said: ‘If you escape from it, you escape from a tremendous thing; / otherwise, I do not think you will pass onward’—meaning, if you escape from the questioning of the grave. The people began to weep. I never saw them weep over anything as they wept that day.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره البرديجي في الأسماء المفردة من الطبقة الأولى وقيل هو بالغين المعجمة قال وقيل لا صحبة له وقال سعيد بن عبد العزيز كان يكون يبيت لهيا وكان من أصحاب معاذ بن جبل ولا يعرف من هو أبوه وأخرجه بن أبي خيثمة
records.english: al-Bardījī mentioned him among the unique names of the first class. It is also said to be written with pointed ghayn. He said, ‘It is said that he had no companionship.’ Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said that he used to spend the night at Luhayā and was one of the companions of Muʿādh ibn Jabal. It is not known who his father was. Ibn Abī Khaythamah included him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
قال البخاري له صحبة وذكره بن سعد في طبقة أهل الخندق روى الترمذي عن بن أبي عمر عن بن عيينة عن عبد الملك بن نوفل عن عصام المزني عن أبيه وكانت له صحبة قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بعث جيشا قال إذا رأيتم مسجدا أو سمعتم مؤذنا فلا تقتلوا أحدا هكذا أورده مختصرا وأخرجه سعيد بن منصور في السنن وأبو داود عنه وأخرجه النسائي في السير من السنن عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن وأخرجه الطبراني في المعجم الكبير من طريق أحمد بن حنبل وحامد بن يحيى البلخي ثلاثتهم عن سفيان بن عيينة بهذا السند مثله إلى قوله فلا تقتلوا أحدا وزاد فبعثنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في سرية وأمرنا بذلك فخرجنا نسير بأرض تهامة فأدركنا رجلا يسوق ظعائن فعرضنا عليه الإسلام فقلنا أمسلم أنت قال وما الإسلام فأخبرناه فإذا هو لا يعرفه قال فإن لم أفعل فما أنتم صانعون فقلنا نقتلك قال فهل أنتم منتظرون حتى أدرك الظعائن فقلنا نعم ونحن مدركوهم قال فخرج فإذا امرأة في هودجها فقال أسلمي حبيش قبل انقطاع العيش فقالت أسلم عشرا وتسعا تتري ثم قالت
أتذكر إذ طالبتكم فوجدتكم
بحلية أو أدركتكم بالخوانق
ألم يك حقا أن ينول عاشق
تكلف إدلاج السري والودائق
فلا ذنب لي قد قلت إذ أهلنا معا
أثيبي بود قبل إحدى المضايق
أثيبي بود قبل أن تشحط النوى
وينأى الأمير بالحبيب المفارق ثم أتانا فقال شأنكم فقربناه فضرنا عنقه فنزلت الأخرى من هودجها فجثت عليه حتى ماتت
records.english: al-Bukhārī said he had companionship; Ibn Saʿd placed him in the class of the people of the Trench. Al-Tirmidhī narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmar, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Nawfal, from ʿIṣām al-Muzanī, from his father, who had companionship. He said: Whenever the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم dispatched an army, he would say, ‘If you see a mosque or hear a caller to prayer, do not kill anyone.’ Al-Tirmidhī cited it in this abbreviated form. Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr transmitted it in al-Sunan, and Abū Dāwūd transmitted it from him. Al-Nasāʾī transmitted it in al-Siyar within al-Sunan from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr by way of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Ḥāmid ibn Yaḥyā al-Balkhī. All three narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah with this chain, in the same form through the words ‘do not kill anyone,’ then added: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent us on a detachment and instructed us accordingly. We set out traveling in the land of Tihāmah and caught up with a man driving women riding in litters. We presented Islam to him and asked, ‘Are you a Muslim?’ He said, ‘What is Islam?’ We told him, and it became clear that he did not know it. He asked, ‘If I do not do so, what will you do?’ We said, ‘We will kill you.’ He said, ‘Will you wait until I catch up with the women in the litters?’ We said, ‘Yes,’ though we were already overtaking them. He went forth, and when he reached a woman in her litter he said, ‘Farewell, Ḥubaysh, before life is cut off.’ She replied, ‘Farewell ten times and nine, one after another.’ Then she said: ‘Do you remember when I pursued you and found you / at Ḥalyah, or overtook you at al-Khawāniq? / Was it not right that a lover should attain his wish, / who undertook night travel and hardships? / I bear no fault; I said when our people were together: / repay love before one of the narrow passes. / Repay love before distance carries us far / and the commander takes the departing beloved away.’ He then came to us and said, ‘Do as you wish.’ We brought him near and struck off his head. The other woman descended from her litter, threw herself upon him, and remained there until she died.
